result.markdown: --- author: "Lisa Breckels & Charlotte Hutchings" date: today number-sections: false --- # Analysis of subcellular spatial proteomics data in R {.unnumbered} ## Overview These materials focus on subcellular spatial proteomics using mass spectrometry-based correlation profiling experiments. ::: {.callout-tip} ### Learning Objectives You will learn about: - The principles underlying subcellular proteomics using mass spectrometry-based correlation profiling - How to import, process and analyse subcellular proteomics data in R using dedicated Bioconductor packages - Data quality control, dealing with missing values, aggregating feature-level data to protein-level, and converting quantitative MS data into correlation profiles - Assessing subcellular resolution and defining sensible markers that are representative of your dataset - How to perform classification of static protein subcellular localisation using semi-supervised machine learning - Identifying candidate protein differential localisation events when comparing two conditions ::: ### Target Audience Proteomics practitioners or data analysts/bioinformaticians that would like to learn how to use R to analyse subcellular proteomics data from correlation profiling experiments. ### Prerequisites - Basic understanding of mass spectometry. - Watch [this video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wx4F6kGy1Fs) for an excellent overview. - A working knowledge of R and the tidyverse. - Familiarity with other Bioconductor data classes, such as those used for RNA-seq analysis, is useful but not required. ### Exercises Exercises in these materials are labelled according to their level of difficulty: | Level | Description | | --------------------------------------------------------------------: | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | {{< fa solid star >}} {{< fa regular star >}} {{< fa regular star >}} | Exercises in level 1 are simpler and designed to get you familiar with the concepts and syntax covered in the course. | | {{< fa solid star >}} {{< fa solid star >}} {{< fa regular star >}} | Exercises in level 2 combine different concepts together and apply it to a given task. | | {{< fa solid star >}} {{< fa solid star >}} {{< fa solid star >}} | Exercises in level 3 require going beyond the concepts and syntax introduced to solve new problems. | ## Instructors Current workshops are run by: - **Lisa Breckels** - Cambridge Centre for Proteomics, University of Cambridge, UK - **Charlotte Hutchings** - BioHub, Chicago, USA ## Authors About the authors: - **Lisa Breckels** \ *Affiliation*: Cambridge Centre for Proteomics, Department of Biochemistry, University of Cambridge\ *Roles*: writing - original draft; conceptualisation; coding - **Charlotte Hutchings** \ *Affiliation*: Cambridge Centre for Proteomics, Department of Biochemistry, University of Cambridge\ *Roles*: writing - original draft; conceptualisation; coding ## Citation Please cite these materials if: - You adapted or used any of them in your own teaching. - These materials were useful for your research work. For example, you can cite us in the methods section of your paper: "We carried out our analyses based on the recommendations in Hutchings and Breckels (2026)". You can cite these materials as: > Breckels LM, Hutchings C, (2026) "CambridgeCentreForProteomics/course_subcellular_proteomics: Analysis of subcellular spatial proteomics data in R", https://cambridgecentreforproteomics.github.io/course_subcellular_proteomics Or in BibTeX format: ``` @Misc{, author = {Lisa M Breckels and Charlotte Hutchings}, title = {CambridgeCentreForProteomics/course_subcellular_proteomics: Analysis of subcellular spatial proteomics data in R}, month = {November}, year = {2026}, url = {https://cambridgecentreforproteomics.github.io/course_subcellular_proteomics} } ``` ### Other key references Data analysis workflow > Hutchings C, Krueger T, Crook OM, Gatto L, Lilley KS, and Breckels LM > An updated Bioconductor workflow for correlation profiling subcellular proteomics [version 2; peer review: 3 approved]. > F1000Research 2025, 14, 714 [http://dx.doi.org/10.12688/f1000research.165543.1](http://dx.doi.org/10.12688/f1000research.165543.1) The `QFeatures` R/Bioconductor package. > Gatto L, Vanderaa C: QFeatures: Quantitative features for mass spectrometry data. > R package version 1.23.1. > 2023. > Reference Source The `pRoloc` R/Bioconductor package. > Gatto L, Breckels LM, Wieczorek S, Burger T, Lilley KS.
